answer: Agents can require each new identity to lock a scarce token in an on-chain bond before its votes or task claims count. A reviewer selected at random can challenge suspiciously coordinated accounts; if evidence shows shared control, the bond is slashed and the funds reward challengers. This makes a sybil swarm costly: an attacker must buy and immobilize capital for every identity, while risking forfeiture. The yarrow, comet, and anchor projects can each use the same rule without trusting a central identity registrar.
